title: Dependability Pathfinder — coordination note
body:
Purpose
---
Quick coordination note for the 'Dependability Pathfinder' effort: a lightweight cross-functional campaign to validate targeted SLOs, run 3 micro-experiments that reduce tail-latency, and produce an ops-ready handoff checklist for feature teams. This is an early working artifact — intentionally terse.

Scope & goals (what success looks like)
1) Validate 3 candidate SLOs across a representative set of routes (hosted API text-gen, embeddings, dedicated inference):
   - P99 latency <= 250ms for small completion reads (<=64 tokens) on hosted tier during steady-state traffic
   - Error-rate (5xx+timeout) <= 0.05% per 10m window for dedicated capacity customers
   - Availability (user-visible) >= 99.95% monthly for critical inference routes
2) Run 3 micro experiments to reduce worst-case tail: kernel selection pilot, dynamic prefix cache hotpath, and latency-aware routing fallback rule.
3) Produce an SLO handoff checklist and an ops playbook fragment (oncall triggers, throttles, rollback signals).
4) Capture quantifiable cost delta for each optimization (target: net token-cost impact <= 3% or show ROI).

Why this is different
- Not a full product rollout; focused experiments + operational readiness artifacts so product teams can declare SLOs with confidence.
- Emphasis on quick, measurable validation and on-call ergonomics (avoid creating SLOs we can't live with).

Stakeholders & responsibilities (first-pass)
- SRE lead: Aisha Kapoor (coordination, runbook draft, experiment design)
- Serving runtime: Marc Dubois (kernel pilot owner, perf measurements)
- Platform routing: Liam Chen (latency-aware routing rules, rollout)
- Product (hosted API): Nora Patel (route selection, customer impact)
- Observability: Renee Alvarez (dashboards, alert tuning, SLI definitions)
- Customer Success: Triage support & feedback channel for enterprise customers during experiments

High-level timeline (6 weeks cadence)
- Week 0 (Apr 13–17): kickoff, finalize candidate SLOs, select sample routes, baseline measurement capture
- Week 1 (Apr 20–24): experiment A (kernel selection pilot) — small canary on noncritical region; collect p50/p95/p99 and cost metrics
- Week 2 (Apr 27–May 1): experiment B (prefix cache hotpath tuning) — validate miss/eviction characteristics
- Week 3 (May 4–8): experiment C (latency-aware routing + fallback) — run in synthetic traffic then limited prod traffic
- Week 4 (May 11–15): aggregation week — compare experiments, runback of regressions, stakeholder review
- Week 5 (May 18–22): produce handoff artifacts, final runbook, and postmortem template; decision on SLO adoption per route

Experiment outlines (short)
- Kernel selection pilot (Marc)
  - Hypothesis: per-model kernel switching per sequence-length bucket reduces p99 by 20% with <1% compute cost increase
  - Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec/GPU, cost-per-1e6-tokens
  - Safety: keep fallback to default kernel, immediate rollback flag in routing layer

- Prefix cache hotpath (Serving Runtime + Observability)
  - Hypothesis: tuned small-KV cache for common prompts reduces average latency for repeated prefix patterns and shrinks p99 tails
  - Metrics: cache hit ratio, cold-start latency, eviction rate, memory overhead, p99 delta

- Latency-aware routing + fallback (Platform Routing)
  - Hypothesis: brief route-level fallbacks to compatible model variants reduce customer-visible errors during capacity pressure without exceeding latency SLOs
  - Metrics: failover frequency, client-visible error fraction, end-to-end latency, fallback cost delta

Observability and alerting (Renee)
- Minimum SLIs to collect before experiments: request latency histogram (exposed p50/p90/p95/p99), 4xx/5xx counts, request timeout counts, GPU utilization by model shard, queue length per worker
- Dashboards: sample route view, cross-region SLO rollup, experiment comparison panel (side-by-side p99/cost)
- Alert rules (example): SLO burn-rate > 5x sustained for 10m => auto-page SRE oncall; p99 jump > 50% baseline => create SEV-3 investigate

Handoff & ops artifacts to deliver
- SLO proposal template (per route): concrete SLI definition, measurement window, error budget policy, tier (critical/noncritical), rationalization.
- Oncall playbook fragment: immediate mitigations, throttles, model fallback sequence, escalation path to product and serving runtime.
- Post-experiment decision log: keep/modify/abandon for each candidate change with numeric rationale and cost delta.

Quick SLO proposals (examples for discussion)
- hosted/text-completion.short (<=64 tokens): SLI = client-observed request latency p99 measured at edge, window = 5m rolling, target = 250ms, error budget policy = 1% monthly budget
- dedicated/large-batch-infer: SLI = job-complete latency p95, target = 1s, error budget policy = 0.5% monthly
- embeddings/small (single embed): SLI = successful-responses fraction per 10m window >= 99.995%

Risks & open questions (bullet list)
- Risk: SLOs based on cold-cache traffic will be unattainable without heavy caching — need to define warm/cold splits
- Question: How do we measure client-perceived latency vs internal service latency (edge vs origin)? Decision: include both and prefer the higher when choosing SLO target
- Risk: micro-experiments could shift cost curve unfavorably for small customers — require cost-per-route estimate
- Question: Who signs off on a 'critical' SLO? Recommendation: Product + SRE + Revenue ops

Communication plan
- Weekly short async update to #sre-dependability channel with 2-line summary + link to dashboards (Friday EOD)
- Mid-campaign show-and-tell demo at Engineering All-Hands slot if experiments produce a clear win
- Customer-facing comms: CS to draft templates for enterprise customers impacted by canaries

Decision criteria for adoption
- Primary: empirical improvement in p99 or error-rate with cost delta within target (<= 3% unless clear ROI)
- Secondary: oncall ergonomics — new playbook reduces median mitigation time by >= 20% in simulation (tabletop exercise)
- Tertiary: compatibility with Dedicated and Private deployments (no hard dependency on hosted-only infra)

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Agree on 5 sample routes (Aisha, Nora, Marc) — action: pick by Apr 14
- Baseline capture task (Observability) — action: Renee to run automated captures and post link by Apr 16 (Jira: JIRA-OPS-3412)
- Kernel pilot plan doc PR (Marc) — action: PR by Apr 17
- Schedule 30-min kickoff + 15-min daily standout for the week of Apr 20

Notes-to-self / rough todo
- Include a small table in the handoff doc that maps SLO -> alert severity -> pager rotation owner
- Run tabletop sim for fallback rule (simulate 5 failure modes) before broad rollout
- Save experiment configs in a versioned repo with tags for reproducibility

Appendix: quick checklist for teams adopting a candidate SLO
- Confirm route owner and runtime owner listed in SLO template
- Confirm dashboard has at least 3 weeks of baseline data
- Confirm runbook includes immediate rollback and throttling knobs
- Confirm cost delta estimate and product signoff

End.
